value.definition: processor seconds a program has spent running

invariants.statement: Seconds spent on more than one processor at once add together.
A program waiting for disk or for a lock spends none.
What a run cost is asked in burned seconds.
A child that has been reaped has its seconds added to its parent's.

value.definition: time that went by while a program ran

invariants.statement: Elapsed time counts while a program waits as well as while a program runs.
Elapsed time under burned time means the work ran on more than one processor.
How long a person waited is asked in elapsed time.
A ceiling on elapsed time bounds waiting rather than bounding processor time.

value.definition: how many threads were runnable or waiting on disk, averaged over a stretch

invariants.statement: Load counts a thread waiting on disk the same as a thread waiting for a processor.
Load above the number of processors is no processor shortage on its own.
The three numbers are averaged over one, five and fifteen minutes.
A load average is of the host rather than of any one program.

value.definition: time work waited for a processor that work could have used

invariants.statement: Stall is the kind that says whether a shortage hurt.
A host fully busy with nothing waiting stalls none.
The kernel keeps stall for each cgroup as well as for the host.

value.definition: time a program was held off a processor by its own ceiling

invariants.statement: Throttling is a ceiling being kept rather than a host being short.
A program is throttled while processors elsewhere are idle.
The kernel counts both how often a program was throttled and for how long.
A ceiling nothing is ever throttled against is a ceiling nothing reached.

value.definition: the part of a processor a program spent over a stretch of time

invariants.statement: A percentage states whether it is of one processor or of every processor.
A program on eight processors reaches eight hundred percent of one.
Utilization is worked out from burned seconds over elapsed time.
A host at full utilization with nothing waiting is a host being used well.
